properties.name: Behavioural state and its transitions are modellable, distinct from lifecycle status
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-07, from the UAF audit: there is no state machine anywhere in the schema, and a whole UAF model-kind column depends on one.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES THIS A REAL GAP RATHER THAN A NAMING ONE: reflow2 has plenty of `status` fields — a Requirement is proposed/accepted/deferred/dropped/met, a Capability is planned/realized/verified, a Verification is planned/passing/failing. Every one of those is a LIFECYCLE status: where a design element has got to in its own maturation. None of them is a BEHAVIOURAL state: a mode the designed thing is in while it operates. And no transition is modelled between any of them — the enums are values, not a graph, so even the lifecycles cannot be projected as a state diagram.

WHAT CANNOT BE SAID TODAY: that a detector is in acquiring / idle / faulted; that a vehicle is in launch / cruise / re-entry; that a protocol connection is in handshake / established / draining; which event causes which transition; which states are safe to be interrupted in. A state view is not expressible, and neither is "what modes must this interface work across".

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND reflow2: reflow2 is a request-response tool with no operating modes to speak of, so the absence costs nothing here and everything on anything with modes. Anthony's own current case is one — a beamline instrument has states, and the analysis stack behaves differently in each.

NOT SPECIFIED HERE: whether states attach to Components, Capabilities or both; whether a transition is an edge or a node; and whether lifecycle status should be unified with behavioural state or kept firmly apart. Kept apart is the likelier answer and is still a decision, not an assumption.
